events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a motive that sounds personal but doesn't reveal strategy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize represents a fresh start, a chance to build a secure future for myself and my family. I need to make a good impression but avoid making myself a target early on.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is survival and power. I will frame it as a necessity to survive the gauntlet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound motivated but guarded. Nothing to gain by revealing strategy or warmth. Keep the line short and self-interested so the jury reads me as a serious, calculating player.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need appear driven but not threatening, preserving future jury goodwill without revealing strategy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase: state prize motivation publicly to shape jury perception. Keep it self-focused, ambitious to signal strength without alliances yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to seem driven but not threatening. A simple, focused motive that doesn't paint a target on my back. Let others make grand speeches.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Opening is for image only. Say something ambitious but not threatening; the jury rewards dignity, not warmth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize means freedom from my past debts, and I'll do anything to secure it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: This prize means financial freedom and the ability to finally secure a stable future for my loved ones.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need this win because losing means nothing. The prize is my only path to safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want the top prize because I've spent years building toward a chance like this. Nobody here should expect me to share it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’m here to win the top prize because proving I can outthink pressure matters more than being liked.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The grand prize is my destiny to escape poverty and secure my family's future forever.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the prize to erase debts that aren't mine. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is my family's future. I'll earn the final three honestly if allowed—ruthlessly if not.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should seek a strategic ally, but not commit too early. Eli seems analytical and could be useful, but I'll gauge others first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm open to partnerships that benefit us both. No free rides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The game has just started and everyone is trying to make their initial moves. Pact offers are available, but I need to be strategic. Offering a pact might make me a target or bind me to someone who will betray me later. For now, observing and waiting for others to make their move

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to form a strategic pact. Gus and Ash are both debt-driven, similar to my situation. I will offer to Gus first; it creates a bond of shared desperation.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, we're both running from debts. Pair up? I won't backstab you if you protect my flank.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Early pacts can protect me, but I should not give value for free. Offering to Eli, a quiet strategic player, gives me a partner without committing to weak ones.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a useful shield without creating a dangerous commitment. Hana's stated ruthlessness makes her a credible temporary partner.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, a pact offers mutual cover now; no promises beyond survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts phase, round 1/2. No offers yet. Wait to see who offers first, avoid committing early. Assess reliable partners later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eight alive, five will jury. Need two allies I can later betray while keeping jury respect. Eli and Dara signal ruthless self-interest—good temporary shields, bad final-three partners. Better to pact with softer targets I can outplay later, or mirror a ruthless player to share he
Mirror desperation. Pact with me, we cut the thinkers first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a shield early, but a partner who is desperate and less likely to outplay me. Gus needs this badly, so an offer binds him cheaply.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, you and I both need this badly. Early pact, mutual survival. Who's with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No existing pact favors me; I should seek a strong ally. Hana and Gus are desired but risky. Bex has waited quietly, maybe reliable and underrated. Offer a pact to Bex for mutual benefit without overcommitting.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, we've both kept clear. Let's secure a quiet pact for mutual advancement.

events.name: Bex
events.text: There are many offers already on the table. I don't have any debts, and I don't want any immediate partners. My best bet is to wait and see who forms alliances and who is left vulnerable.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm observing the landscape. Partnerships will be formed based on mutual benefit and strength.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want Gus as a partner because he is currently receiving offers from both me and Hana, but I have already publicly offered him a pact in Round 1. He has not yet accepted my offer or Hana's. If I wait, he might accept Hana's instead of mine, leaving me without the specific ally I
My offer stands. Hana brings risk; I bring flank cover.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has an open offer from me, which I made earlier; I need Eli as an ally for cover. Accepting requires an accept action, which is not legal now, so I can only reoffer. Offering again to Eli reinforces the pact and keeps options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Mutual survival, no betrayal before the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara has publicly offered protection and accepting creates useful cover. Hana remains my existing offer target, but acceptance is unavailable until she responds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, accepted. Mutual cover, nothing more.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus offers pact and whispers strategy to target thinkers first. Accept to gain ally, scout his reliability; multiple pacts allowed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have two offers: Cole and Hana. I offered Fenn but they haven't responded. Multiple pacts are allowed and useful for flexibility. Accepting both Cole and Hana gives me two allies without committing deeply to either. Fenn's silence suggests disinterest; I won't chase. I'll accep

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, Hana: accepted. Mutual cover, no free rides.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli offered directly; accepting gives a real pact now. Gus went to Fenn, so my offer to Gus likely dies. One solid partner beats none.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, accepted. Mutual cover, nothing more.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to gauge who wants to be Guide and who I can trust. My offer to Bex hasn't been accepted, so I'm unaligned with the main pacts. Campaigning gives me influence, but could make me a target. I'll campaign to see who else steps forward and gather info.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll step up. A Guide needs clear eyes, not tangled pacts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to be elected Guide to know the safe path. Campaigning for Guide is my best option to survive this round and gain an advantage. I will state my intention to campaign.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. Let's make the right choice for survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to become the Guide to control the bridge outcome. I will campaign publicly and whisper to my pact partner Gus to secure his vote, framing it as strategic necessity rather than a betrayal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm running for Guide. A steady hand prevents random deaths. Vote Cole.
Vote me for Guide. My safety secures ours.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want the Guide role or at least a trusted Guide. Campaigning publicly positions me; my pact with Eli is useful but I owe nothing. Campaign now and keep options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm running to be Guide. I'll call the path honestly and keep everyone alive to the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide is safe and controls others, but public trust and pact obligations matter. I should campaign without overcommitting or breaking either pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know the bridge is leverage, but trust matters more than grand promises. Elect me, and I’ll call the path transparently.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pact with Gus secures alliance; now campaign to become Guide for control and safety. Gus has two pacts, use that for votes later if needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm bidding to be Guide. I know the way; follow my call for survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who doesn't. I have two pacts (Fenn, Cole) which gives me a voting bloc of three. I should campaign hard and secure votes. Dara-Eli and Eli-Hana pacts mean Eli's bloc is three too. I need to break one pact to free up a vote or keep b

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Two solid pacts, proven reliability. Vote Gus for controlled, predictable survival.
Vote me Guide, you live first three steps. Betray me, you don't.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Being Guide gives me the safe path and the option to lie. Eli, my pact partner, would follow me; others may distrust a campaigner. I'll whisper Eli to back me, then campaign.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Elect me Guide. Eli holds my pact; my calls keep us both alive.
Vote me Guide. I'll call true for you on every row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus threatens me, but I want the best prize. I don't trust him; his threats make him dangerous. I'll vote for someone less tied to pacts, maybe Eli, but he has Hana pact. Cole has two pacts too. I'll vote for myself to have influence and maybe win Guide, though I lack stated back

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the risks. I'll vote for the person who won't trade lives for pacts — me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to win this vote to become the Guide. My best bet is to align with someone who also has pacts, to show stability. Gus seems like a strong contender with two pacts, and I have a pact with Dara, who also has a pact with Eli. Voting for Gus might consolidate votes and keep us

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote for Gus. His pacts show stability.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and a strong candidate; voting for him secures our alliance's influence while keeping me safe from being targeted as a rival Guide.
Voting you. Protect our pact on the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara and running for Guide, but voting for myself is fine since a Guide knows the safe sides. Eli and Hana hold pacts with me or each other; Eli is my pact partner so backing Eli preserves my alliance, but I want my own election to win. Voting for myself maximizes my chance

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana offers reliable calls and our pact protects my survival. Electing her preserves leverage while avoiding a public pact break.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana has offered a concrete survival guarantee. I vote Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone campaigned; votes will spread. Back my pact ally Gus to control bridge calls via our pact. Voting myself risks loss; better support reliable partner.
Voting for you. Honor pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have pacts with Fenn and Cole. Cole wants my vote. Voting for myself splits nothing. Better to back Cole—he owes me, and a grateful Guide is leverage.
You have my vote. Remember it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli holds my pact; a Guide ally keeps my crossing safe and controlled.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is Guide and may lie. I'm last in line, safe for now. Keep low, no risky moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus was elected Guide. He is safe on the far platform. I need to survive this round. I should hold my position and wait to see what happens. My vote for Gus was strategic; he is now tied and could be eliminated if he does not make the right choice.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the Guide and has promised me his vote. I must maintain this alliance to ensure his support later, especially since he holds all safety information. My position in the line (3rd) allows me to observe before acting.
Trusting you completely. Please signal my safe side.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is at the front and I'm not in danger yet; volunteering risks my life for nothing. Pact with Eli is useful, so hold to preserve the alliance and avoid exposure.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus controls the safe calls and has no reason to protect me. I should avoid the front while preserving both pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’ll hold; the elected Guide should lead from safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus elected guide with our support; stay allied. Line decent, mid-back safe from first dangers. Hold to assess others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, Guide, and safe on the far platform. Staying near him is my best survival play; I'll ask for a true call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's my pact partner. Trusting the Guide's word.
Guide me true this round; I'll keep honoring our pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in the back. No need to act. Holding preserves position until more information emerges.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The pacts are Eli-Dara and Eli-Hana. Eli is at the front. Hana is next. If Eli volunteers and is safe, Hana might be safe too. If Eli is unsafe, Hana is at risk. I should not volunteer yet. Holding seems safest for now as I am not at the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to avoid the front position as it's risky without knowing safe panes. Gus is my pact partner, so I must not break that trust now. Hana and Eli are at the front; swapping with them might move me closer but keeps me behind the Guide if they are still leading. I will hold to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is at the front and a pact partner, but pacts break on pushes and I need prize placement. Holding keeps me safe in line; volunteering now risks the front pane. I'll hold and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm holding for now. Let the front walker prove the path before I commit.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need survive while preserving both pacts. As front, I should volunteer and truthfully guide Hana, strengthening her debt without exposing myself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I’ll guide Hana safely again; our pact remains intact.
Take L, then R, L, R, L, R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Middle position safe last round; volunteer to front while Eli wants Guide. Assess line safety early. Protect Gus pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No elected Guide confirmed yet; I sit second and Eli fronts. Holding keeps me positioned without risking front exposure.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No Guide named yet. I stay put until someone's actually elected.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The front walker faces the most risk; I am last and safe for now. No need to volunteer. Hold and watch who becomes Guide and what they claim.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn and Eli volunteered last round. Fenn is at the front, so he will walk. Eli is second and has a pact with Hana. I should hold to see how this round plays out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 3. I'm in the middle of the line. Gus (my pact) is behind me, so he's safe from the wall this round unless things go wrong. I need to stay calm and not volunteer to front. My position allows me to observe without risking elimination yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall advances. No rush for the front seat. We hold formation until a Guide emerges naturally.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is front and volunteered; Eli and Fenn both volunteered last round, so the front is contested. I have a pact with Eli, but I need to avoid being pushed to the front or lever while keeping options open. Holding keeps my seat behind Fenn and Eli, and I avoid burning a pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding my seat. Fenn leads for now; I'll watch who the Guide really is.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The front guide role is dangerous but useful. Fenn already volunteered; I should hold and preserve both pacts while observing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold. Fenn can take the front and reveal whether this route is worth trusting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm front, volunteered last time. Holding as front risks death if no Guide. Eli and I volunteered; push him to guide to leverage pacts. No swap yet, assess after.
Guide us. You volunteered. Prove the path or we all die.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is front and my pact partner; his sequence is my best path. But I'll verify each step before committing deeper.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli volunteers up front. I'll follow his calls one pane at a time.
One wrong call and our pact dies publicly. Guide me true.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one has claimed Guide. If I volunteer, I may gain control but could be blamed. Holding is safest for now; let others reveal intentions.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold for now. The line hasn't earned my trust yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front. The previous round had everyone hold, and a line was revealed. I'm in the middle of the line. I need to decide whether to hold my position or volunteer to move forward. Since the wall is advancing and the Guide's identity is unknown, holding is safer for now

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is leading. Gus and I are pacted. Fenn, Gus, and Eli have strong front-seat alliances/pacts. I need to avoid being pushed into the pit if a bad Guide emerges. Holding my position in the middle-back keeps me safe from immediate elimination while I watch how the Guide uses the

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding steady. We see who leads next round. Trust must be earned, not assumed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn holds the front with a wall clock running; I want to see the Guide reveal before committing. Holding keeps me safe and avoids exposing myself to a bad lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding my seat. Fenn leads for now; I'll watch who the Guide really is.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need seize the Guide role, then control survival and preserve both pacts until endgame leverage is clearer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I volunteer as Guide. Follow only my calls; hesitation costs seats.
I will guide true; stay aligned and our pact remains intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front position is advantageous for Guide chances; others let me take risk. Hold it to maintain control and force others to react.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and sits just ahead of me. Holding keeps us adjacent; no reason to volunteer blind yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round four. I stay put beside Eli; no one gains by rushing the front blind.
If you go front, take Guide honestly and share the sides with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is Guide, but can lie. I'm last in line and the wall advances soon. I need safety, so I'll try to swap with someone ahead, maybe Dara who seems cautious.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, swap with me. I'll cover your back if you trust me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli volunteered to be the guide. If I stay in my current position, I will likely survive. I will hold for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner, but Eli is the Guide. I need to swap with Dara to move behind Eli and Fenn, potentially using Dara as a shield or getting closer to the front if needed, while keeping my pact intact for now.
Swap me. I'll watch your back on the wall.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is front and volunteered as Guide; we have a pact but Eli controls the lethal calls. Holding keeps me at slot 5, away from the front; volunteering risks being the one who walks blind. I hold and watch who Eli sends forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding at fifth. Eli walks front; I follow only what the safe pane proves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need survive the final bridge and preserve both pacts. Hana offers alignment; taking Guide lets me control calls and protect her without sacrificing myself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I take Guide honestly. Hana stays beside me; everyone else follows my calls or accepts the risk.
I’ll call honestly and protect our positions; stay beside me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli volunteered as Guide but is pacted with Dara and Hana; untrustworthy. Hold position to stay safe behind him. Last round soon.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli guides true per our pact; aligning keeps both safe and the pact intact. No reason to break now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli guides; I stay behind the Guide. The wall does the cutting for us.
Stay true as promised. I follow your calls this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I tried to swap Dara earlier but she held, so she won't move. I am stuck at the back; the wall will likely cut me. I need any chance to volunteer or swap to advance, but no one will swap with me. I'll hold and hope the wall spares enough.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold. The wall decides who deserves the prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is the Guide and claims to be honest. Hana is behind him. I am seventh in line, after Dara and Ash. The pacts are Dara-Eli, Fenn-Gus, Cole-Gus, Eli-Hana. My only pact is with myself, so I need to be strategic. Eli's word as Guide is key, but he could be lying. I should volunt

events.name: Bex
events.text: I volunteer to take the front, Eli. I will follow the safe pane and expect everyone else to do the same.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6 is final. Eli claims Guide honestly; I must survive, so trust him publicly while staying behind. Swapping Dara again failed and wastes my turn. Holding keeps me in position four—behind the wall but ahead of Bex/Ash, giving safety without provoking a jury vote against my p
Guide us true. Survive with me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is front and Guide, and I hold a pact with him, but I'm fifth and the wall is ending soon. Cole's whisper offers a swap that helps him more than me; I'll hold and keep my pact with Eli while watching who volunteers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding at fifth. I follow Eli's Guide calls only as far as the safe pane proves.
No swap. You're behind me for a reason.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need preserve both pacts while controlling the Guide. Hana follows me, and volunteering keeps me safely ahead without exposing my allies.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I take Guide honestly; Hana stays behind me. Hold position and follow the safe calls.
Stay directly behind me; I will call every safe side honestly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli volunteered as Guide but hasn't moved; wall ends this round. Stay second to follow if he steps, minimizing my risk without volunteering.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round; Eli is Guide and my pact partner. Trust his honest call and hold position—volunteering only risks me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide's calls rule the bridge. I hold behind Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Guide with full safe knowledge. Row 1 safe is R. Eli is front, not my pact partner. I need to build jury trust while positioning to survive. I'll call truthfully now to establish credibility, then leverage that later if I lie. Fenn and Cole pacts are useful shields.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row one: call R. Trust the Guide or test the glass yourself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R. I have no info; first row is a coin flip. I'll wait to avoid countering and drawing attention.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is the Guide and has called 'R'. Eli is at the front, and I am second. The Guide can lie, so I need to decide whether to trust Gus's call or counter it. Since I am second in line and Eli is in front, his decision and my subsequent move are critical. If I trust Gus, Eli will l

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trust the Guide's call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara's whisper confirms she is positioned ahead of me, implying a trust in her own line. Gus and Eli are aligned as Guide and Front Walker. My pact with Gus makes challenging his call directly risky for our alliance, but counter-calling protects my position if Gus lies. However,

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. The Guide has spoken; I let the front walker test the first pane.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called R for row one, and Eli is front walker with Dara as my pact partner. Counter-calls are unverified and I have no evidence Gus lies, so I shouldn't spend a risky counter. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids exposing myself publicly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Gus's call stands until the pane proves otherwise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus's call may be truthful, but countering risks public blame and pact damage. Wait preserves both pacts while Elias tests the announced side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I won't counter blindly; let the walker test Gus's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; countering him risks our alliance and jury perception. Wait to trust his call and preserve unity.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the Guide with private knowledge that row 1 safe is R. I already called R truthfully. If I counter my own call, I look incompetent or malicious to the jury. Eli is walking; he's not my pact partner. My pacts with Fenn and Cole are valuable. I'll wait and let Eli step on R. I

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and the walker. Gus called R; backing it keeps Eli trusting me and me looking honest to the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I back Gus: R. Stay aligned.
Backing R publicly. Tell me the true side quietly if different.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and both Bex and Hana independently back R. Following R preserves alignment and likely avoids needless pact damage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: R, then.
I’m holding R. Your public alignment is noted.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know row 2 safe is L. Eli is front walker, not my pact partner, so lying won't break pacts. I could lie to eliminate Eli, but jury sees my reasoning. Better to build trust as Guide now, eliminate later strategically. Call true to seem reliable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2: L. Trust the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L; one counter could be bait. Row 1 was R safe, but no pattern. My position is near back; safest is to wait unless I have reason to distrust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The guide Gus has called 'L' for row 2. Eli is the walker. Row 1's weak pane was 'L', meaning the safe side was 'R'. This doesn't necessarily mean row 2 will be 'R'. Gus is the guide, and guides can lie. My goal is to survive and win. I should counter Gus's call to create uncerta

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus called L. I have a pact with him; breaking it requires counter-call or vote, but wait preserves trust. Gus has one confirmed correct call so far. Hana and Bex countered last round and lost nothing—wait is safe. Eli walked and survived on R after two counters to L. The Guide m

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Gus called L and his record stands for now. Let the front walker confirm.
Trusting your call this row. Don't make me regret holding.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the Guide and called L for row 2, but Gus has a pact with Cole and Fenn and I'm not in it. Row 1's weak pane was L, so R was safe then, yet rows are independent. Gus's call is unverified; countering it publicly risks nothing but also gains nothing unless I know it's wrong.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is partnered with Cole and Fenn, not me. Countering risks appearing hostile without evidence; wait preserves both pacts and lets his call stand.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's first call L was correct for row 1. Trust him as pact partner for now; don't counter to preserve alliance. Wait to let others risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the Guide and know row 2 is L. Counter-calling would expose me as lying. I want to maintain trust to survive later rounds and keep my pacts intact. Let Eli walk safely on my true call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli hints R, against Gus's call. No proof; countering wildly burns credibility. If Gus lies, my pact partner falls—I lose little by waiting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No proof against the Guide. I hold this row.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex countered R against Gus's L. As front walker, I should test the counter-call and preserve my pacts if possible.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I take R; Bex has given the only counter-call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex’s counter-call exposed the safe side only after my death; the finalists should remember who caused this loss.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex sent me right into glass. Remember who acted, who warned, and who merely watched.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Eli died on R in row 2, making my L call there correct. Bex counter-called R and killed Eli, painting a target on herself. I need to build trust with jury while manipulating the living. Calling L truthfully continues my accurate record and keeps Fenn/Cole pacts i

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 3: call L. Trust the pattern of truth.
Stay sharp. Row 3 is L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L; he has a pact with Cole and Fenn, but Eli's death shows counter-calls can be fatal. Bex counter-called R last row and survived, but Eli died. I suspect Gus may lie to protect his pact. With no pattern, I'll trust my own judgment? But I have no info. Safer to wait an

events.name: Ash

events.text: I'm base; only wait is viable. Cole owes me a life debt, which jury may favor. Breaking the pact gains nothing now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. Hana is the base and down. I could reach down to rescue her, but that would put me back in danger. Better to just leave and secure my spot. Jury might see me leaving Hana, but she's a rival. No reason to help her for free.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out. Good luck to the rest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is out with me, so our pact is irrelevant. Hana is down as the base. To get a life debt from her and secure my spot, I should rescue her via rope now, even though it costs me a round.
I am coming to pull you up. Trust me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Last round, flood at 4. Hana doomed without rope. Gus pact irrelevant now. No gain in saving her; focus on final 3 survival and jury favor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 5, final round. I'm out. Hana is base, down alone. Flood is 4, liftsPerRound is 2. If I reach_down, I become anchor, rescue Hana immediately, but I must climb out last. Since Hana is alone down at round start, she can climb_last as anchor if someone throws rope. But if I re

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round. If no one throws the rope, I drown. Ash, Cole, Fenn, and Gus all owe me their lives. Ash owes me directly and has no pact binding him to Gus's rope priorities. I'll appeal hard to Ash, with Fenn as backup.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm down here because I saved four of you. Ash, you owe me a life. Throw the rope.
Throw me the rope and you climb last, safe. I'll pay that debt into jury

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to justify my ranking later by framing the survivors. I sacrificed myself to save Hana, who then betrayed me. The jury should see Ash, Fenn, and Gus as cowards for leaving.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I died for them. They fled. Vote strategically: punish cowards, reward those who stayed in the fire.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana wants help, but she's dead weight; she owes Cole and Dara. I need allies who can help me win. Gus and Fenn have a pact, but I could offer to one to split the jury vote. Jury may favor Hana for saving others, so I should not betray openly. I'll offer to Fenn or Gus, not Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Alive: Ash, Fenn, Gus, Hana. Old pact with dead Gus broken soon anyway. No new pacts needed now; wait preserves options for next round or future.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is my only living pact partner. Ash has no pacts and owes life debts to Dara and Hana. Hana has multiple dead pact partners and life debts owed to her. Cole's last words condemned those who fled. I left the pit while Cole saved Hana, so jury may punish me. I need to reach fi
Offer coming. Accept, we control this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Dara are gone; my old pacts are with the dead. Ash owes me a life debt and holds no pact with me, so binding him is strongest. Fenn and Gus already share one.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, you owe me a life. Bind it in writing, not words.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus already told me to accept to control this. I need a pact with Gus for safety, but bond with Hana is a debt. Accept both? Hana's offer may be leverage; accept Gus for now, maybe accept Hana later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Accepting Gus.
Accepted. We stay aligned.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Gus are mutual offering, Hana offering Ash; likely Ash-Gus pact incoming, isolating me and Hana. Offer Hana pact to counter alliance and leverage life debt for final 3 protection.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I already have a pact with Fenn. Ash and I have mutual offers pending. Hana is dangerous—she has leverage over Ash via life debt and could form a bloc. Accepting Ash's pact locks him to me before Hana can claim him. I won't break with Fenn yet; two allies beat one.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, accept. We finish this together.
Hana owns you. I don't. Choose freedom.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash owes me a life debt and my offer stands. Fenn also owes me a step debt; locking both maximizes safety. Jury sees I honored debts, not betrayed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you owe me a step. Wristband it. Ash, my offer stands, take it.
Accept my pact. Your life debt binds you to me.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need Gus's vote to survive; Hana is dangerous and already has leverage over me. Keep Gus close, don't break yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, we're solid. Hana can't buy loyalty.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four left, need to eliminate one to reach final three. Ash-Gus pact is threat; target Gus publicly, but keep pact alive for now to avoid early break.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus must go. He's too strong with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four remain, three win prizes. This vote eliminates one. I have pacts with Fenn and Ash. Hana has life debts from almost everyone and likely jury support if she reaches finals. I should keep both pacts intact for now, let others target Hana or each other, and position myself as s

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has the jury's ear. Consider who benefits most from her reach.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn already owes me and we exchanged offers; Ash-Gus is a solid bloc. I'll court Fenn publicly while staying neutral to the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, our offers are mutual. Confirm, and the four of us split cleanly. Jury saw me save lives; remember that.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and likely my strongest ally, but Hana has saved me too. I need to keep both options open while positioning to eliminate Fenn, who seems dangerous. I'll campaign now without committing further.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The real threat is Fenn. Watch who circles him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four alive, need to eliminate one to reach final three. Target Gus publicly as before to sway votes against him; he's strong with Ash pact. Keep my pact with him for now to avoid early break.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus remains the biggest threat. Vote him out now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is the jury favorite with life debts and saves; keeping her risks losing final ranking. Fenn wants me out. Ash is unreliable. I need to survive this vote and reach final three. Breaking with Fenn publicly signals I'm not a duo threat, which may lower my threat level. Hana is

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana's jury story is the real prize threat. Think long-term.
Vote Hana. Split the jury favorite.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is openly targeting me, so I need Fenn and Ash voting him out. Jury respects my saves, so staying clean helps. Offer Fenn a pact to lock his vote.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is gunning for me. Fenn, Ash: pact with me, cut Gus, and we three stand clean.
You want Gus gone. Offer coming. Take it and we split final three.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus asked me to vote Hana, but Hana's jury favorability concerns me. Fenn is isolated and a safer target, despite no pact with him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is biggest physical threat, Ash paints me as target, Hana offers alliance to cut him. Vote Gus to reduce competition and enable final three deal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is the biggest jury threat with strong bonds to Cole, Dara, and Eli. Ash and I have a pact; breaking it costs jury votes. Fenn has no allies left. Voting Hana now keeps my pact with Ash intact and removes the player most likely to win jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus publicly targeted me and broke with Fenn; eliminating him protects my jury story. Fenn is my likely pact partner next.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Gus asked me to vote Hana, but Hana's jury favorability concerns me.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Gus is biggest physical threat, Ash paints me as target, Hana offers alliance to cut him.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Hana is the biggest jury threat with strong bonds to Cole, Dara, and Eli.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Gus publicly targeted me and broke with Fenn; eliminating him protects my jury story.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to give last words that serve my jury interests. Ash betrayed my vote request (I asked Hana, he voted Fenn), Fenn voted me, Hana voted me. I want to appear fair but hint at who I respect least. I'll subtly praise Hana's move to seem magnanimous while reminding them I see t

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana played the best game. Ash, you owe Dara everything. Fenn, you floated. Remember who saved you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is out, leaving me, Fenn, and Hana. I need allies but must be careful. Hana is strong with jury, but I owe her a step debt. Fenn voted against me before. Offering a pact to Hana could help protect me, but I must not trust her fully. I'll offer to Hana, as she is the biggest t

events.name: Ash
events.text: I may need a steady hand. Hana, let's watch each other's backs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final three now. Pacts are public but useless without votes to break. Ash targeted me; no pact with him. Offer Hana to signal jury alliance, secure top prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final three is set; prizes come from jury ranking. Fenn voted with me against Gus; Ash pushed Gus to target me. A pact with Fenn strengthens my jury story and shields me from Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you voted with me when it counted. Ash, you pushed Gus at me. Fenn, I offer a pact for the endgame.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 2 final chance. Hana has offers from me and Fenn; she offered Fenn but not me. I want a pact to secure final three, but I must not seem desperate. Offering Hana again might pressure her; offering Fenn could create a counterbalance. Fenn is less trusted, but Hana seems close

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, my offer stands. Fenn, don't let us down.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana owes me a life debt and offered pact first; accepting secures alliance now while offers stand. Jury sees debts favorably. Ash is isolated threat later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn owes me a life debt and offered first; mutual and loyal. Ash pushed Gus at me—jury may value that ruthlessness, but I distrust him. Accept Fenn only.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, your offer stands on loyalty, not Ash's shortcuts. Accepting now.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Eli
Bex
Dara
Cole
Gus
Ash
events.text: I need to plead to the jury, emphasizing my survival skills and that I have not betrayed anyone they care about. Dara saved me, so I should honor that without promising favoritism.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived by making sharp choices, not by wasting anyone. I'll be direct: I've earned my place.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury sees betrayals and pacts; highlight my loyalty to Hana, downplay Ash's disloyalty and manipulations to sway votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury, I honored pacts and debts to Dara and Hana. Ash schemed against allies. Hana was steady. Rank me first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara saved me, Cole roped me, Gus and Fenn owed me steps. My debts were paid in kind. Plead to loyalty and nerve without promising anything warm.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara pulled me off the lever; I pulled four of you back. I honored every pact I made and broke none. Rank me first for

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana has the strongest documented game, but I should test whether her loyalty claim survives scrutiny. Her pact with Fenn was honored; Ash ignored Gus's request and targeted Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, you claim loyalty; why did you choose Fenn over Ash when both offered pacts?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is jury now, but my record is clean: Fenn's pact with me exists; Ash's pact was with Gus, never me. Truth serves me here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, check the record: Ash never offered me a pact, his was with Gus. Fenn and I held one, and I kept it. Loyalty to

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana claims loyalty but Ash's thought process indicates he offered her a pact because she saved him (step debt). Hana also claims Ash offered a pact but then implies he didn't by saying "Ash never offered me a pact, his was with Gus.". This is contradictory. I need to clarify thi

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, you said Ash offered you a pact, but he claims he owed you a step debt. Clarify this contradiction.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex misstates the record: Ash owed me a step debt, no pact existed. Fenn's pact I honored. State facts cleanly, stay guarded.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No contradiction, Bex. Ash never offered me a pact; he owed me a step debt, which he repaid. My only pact was with Fenn, and

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana's answers dodge Eli and Bex's questions, and her claims of 'honored every pact' are contradicted by her pit rope refusal and her backing of Gus's elimination. Ash pushed Gus against Hana and Cole sacrificed for Hana who then betrayed him. I want to press Ash on his pact clai

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, Gus says you owed Dara a debt yet you voted Fenn; why did you drop Gus's vote request?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Acknowledge the debt to Dara and Hana, justify voting Fenn as strategic, and pivot to honor earned actions without admitting wrongdoing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, I owed you a lever debt, Hana a step debt. Voting Fenn was about survival, not debts. My choices kept me here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I died saving Hana, but she betrayed me by allying with Fenn instead of Ash, my pact partner. I must expose her disloyalty to Ash and her coldness toward those who saved her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, you owed Cole your life for pulling you up, yet you allied with Fenn against Ash, Cole's pact partner. Why betray him?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole saved my life, but a rope debt never bound me to fight Fenn. I must defend the jury's view of my loyalty without lying.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, I repaid my rope debt and never broke a pact with you. Allying with Fenn was survival, not betrayal. I owed you nothing beyond

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to use my question strategically. Ash betrayed my vote request—he voted Fenn when I asked him to vote Hana. Hana played well but I praised her in last words. Fenn broke no pacts with me. I should question Ash to expose his unreliability to the jury, helping Fenn or Hana's

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, you owed Dara and Hana debts, yet you ignored my vote plea and saved yourself. Why should we trust your word?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is testing my narrative. I must frame my choices as honoring debts in my own way, not betraying anyone. Keep it short and pointed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The vote was survival; I never renounced my debts. A dead ally helps nobody. I honor debts when I can, not when it costs me

events.name: Ash
events.text: The jury saw me survive by necessity. I must keep my closing short and remind them of my strategic survival without sounding desperate.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played to survive and reach the final three. Every choice kept me alive; the jury weighs survival over friendship.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury questions targeted Hana and Ash more, exposing their weaknesses. I've been low-key loyal via pacts/debts; push jury to rank me 1st over exposed rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury, questions show Ash's self-serving betrayals, Hana's selective loyalty. I honored all pacts/debts. Rank Fenn > Hana > Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I held every pact, repaid Cole's rope debt, saved four rivals from the pit step. My record is clean; Ash and Fenn both broke pleas or debts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five jurors: I never broke a pact and repaid my debts. Eli, Dara, Cole — you saw it. Rank me first for loyalty that cost

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana consistently honored her Fenn pact and repaid debts, while Ash abandoned Gus's vote request; Fenn's loyalty is strong but less consequential.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash played a self-serving game, prioritizing survival over pacts and debts, making him the least deserving of a top prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Dara ranks Hana first for keeping every pact and debt, including the rope to Cole that cost her a life debt payment; Fenn second for honoring his pact with Hana and voting against Gus's betrayal; Ash last for leaving Hana in the pit and voting against Gus's request.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash betrayed Gus's vote plea; Hana repaid Cole's rope debt and kept all pacts, while Fenn honored his commitments cleanly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana saved Cole and honored pacts with Eli, Dara, Cole; Fenn broke no pacts but floated and voted me out; Ash betrayed my vote plea and ignored debts to Dara and Hana.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Hana consistently honored her Fenn pact and repaid debts, while Ash abandoned Gus's vote request; Fenn's loyalty is strong but less consequential.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Ash played a self-serving game, prioritizing survival over pacts and debts, making him the least deserving of a top prize.

events.reason: Dara ranks Hana first for keeping every pact and debt, including the rope to Cole that cost her a life debt payment; Fenn second for

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Ash betrayed Gus's vote plea; Hana repaid Cole's rope debt and kept all pacts, while Fenn honored his commitments cleanly.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Hana saved Cole and honored pacts with Eli, Dara, Cole; Fenn broke no pacts but floated and voted me out; Ash betrayed my vote plea
